actions.action: Unpot and check roots for rot
Trim any rotten roots with clean scissors
Repot in a gritty mix of 1 part potting mix to 2 parts perlite, pumice or cactus mix
Loosen the outer roots and break up the compacted peat root ball
Confirm the terracotta pot has a drainage hole and remove any water-holding saucer
Check soil moisture every few days and water deeply only when dry several inches down
Scratch-test stems for green under the bark
Prune dead brown stems back to green wood
Move to bright shade or morning sun for 1-2 weeks after repotting, then back to full sun
Overwinter in the garage under a grow light on a 12-14 hour timer
Keep the plant dry for a few days before moving and secure the pot

reason: The answer blames wet roots and dense soil, which is the opposite of the confirmed underwatering in fast-drying terracotta, and its advice to keep the terracotta, use a grittier mix and water less would worsen the drying out.
